zones.what: Lifeboats are mounted at Deck 7; they obstruct the view downward from Decks 8, and partially from Deck 6, while horizon views remain clear.
zones.effect: You cannot see straight down to the water or watch tender operations, but the ocean horizon and ports are visible — the balcony or window feels elevated rather than open to the sea below.
zones.mattersTo: Matters to guests who want the full open-to-the-water feeling or enjoy watching tender loading; does not matter if you care only about horizon views and sunsets.

zones.what: The main pool deck, buffet, and outdoor activity areas are on Deck 11 directly above.
zones.effect: Daytime foot traffic, deck chair dragging, pool sounds, and buffet activity from above can be heard; evenings are quieter once the pool deck closes.
zones.mattersTo: Matters to light sleepers and anyone in the cabin during the day; does not matter if you are out exploring and return only to sleep.

zones.what: The main dining rooms are on Deck 6, three decks below midship Deck 9 cabins.
zones.effect: Dining room activity is far enough below that noise and vibration are typically not noticeable in Deck 9 cabins.
zones.mattersTo: Does not matter for most guests; spacing provides good insulation.

zones.what: The showroom/theatre is on Deck 6 directly above most of Deck 5.
zones.effect: Late-night show sound, applause, and foot traffic during performances can filter down; the theatre typically goes quiet by 11 PM.
zones.mattersTo: Matters to early sleepers or anyone turning in before the second show; does not matter if you attend the shows or stay out late.

zones.what: These cabins are low and aft, near the engine room and propulsion machinery.
zones.effect: A low hum or vibration is noticeable underway, especially at cruising speed; it is constant white noise rather than banging or rattling.
zones.mattersTo: Matters to guests sensitive to vibration or who want absolute quiet; does not matter to those who sleep through white noise or use the cabin only to sleep.

zones.what: Bow thruster operation during docking and maneuvering can be heard and felt in forward cabins on lower decks.
zones.effect: A loud mechanical whine and vibration for a few minutes during port arrivals and departures; it does not occur at sea.
zones.mattersTo: Matters to light sleepers who are in the cabin during early-morning arrivals; does not matter if you sleep heavily or are up and out early.

zones.what: The anchor chain locker is in the bow; anchor drop and retrieval create loud clanking early in the morning at every port.
zones.effect: A brief but very loud mechanical noise at anchor operations, typically between 6 and 8 AM; it lasts a few minutes.
zones.mattersTo: Matters to anyone who values sleeping in at port; does not matter to early risers or those planning to wake for arrival anyway.

zones.what: The main elevator and stair banks run midship through all guest decks.
zones.effect: Midship cabins near the elevators offer maximum convenience but may hear elevator machinery hum, door chimes, and hallway conversation during busy embarkation and port days.
zones.mattersTo: Matters to guests prioritizing quiet over convenience; does not matter to those who value short walks to elevators and public areas.

unknowns: Whether Norwegian Spirit has a hump (balconies cantilevered past the hull line on lower-midship decks) — this hull class predates the era when humps became standard, and I cannot confirm its presence or absence without deck cross-sections.
